hook_text: In 1871 a small hill near the Vaal was claimed by four rulers at once. Then a fifth took it.
clip_script: 1867, Hopetown. A boy picks up a pebble: a diamond. By 1871, on a hill called Colesberg Kopje, diggers discover diamonds that go down and down, inside a pipe of ancient volcanic rock. Suddenly a dusty borderland is worth a fortune. And everyone says it is theirs. The Orange Free State. The Transvaal. The Griqua leader Nicolaas Waterboer. Tswana chiefs. A Natal official, Robert Keate, rules against the Transvaal. Waterboer asks Britain for protection, and in October 1871 Britain takes the lot and names it Griqualand West. The Free State gets ninety thousand pounds. The Griqua, whose claim Britain used, lose their land within a few years. And the hill becomes the Big Hole of Kimberley.
visual_style: A whiteboard hill with four flags planted on it, a gavel coming down, then a fifth flag replacing them all and the hill turning into a deep hole.
pacing: Quick build-up of claims, a beat of silence at the gavel, then a fast twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and decide who really owned the diamond fields.
